visuals: The tall, rugged peaks of the Alborz mountains in Iran under a clear blue sky. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Mountains, deserts, and more mountains! Iran is full of towering peaks and dry plains.

visuals: A vast, dry desert plain in central Iran with sparse vegetation. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Summers are very hot and dry in many areas.

visuals: A snowy mountain landscape in northern Iran with people skiing on the slopes. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: While northern and higher regions can get snowy in winter up to the point where people actually go skiing. Yes, skiing… in the Middle East!

visuals: A panoramic view of the majestic Zagros Mountains in Iran, showing their rocky ridges and deep valleys. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Now for my favorite part: the Zagros Mountains! These rocky giants in western Iran are among the oldest mountain ranges on Earth. You could say they’ve got serious “rock star” status.

visuals: A wild mountain goat standing on a rocky slope in the highlands of Iran. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Wild goats live in the highlands.

visuals: A rare Persian leopard prowling through the rugged hills of an Iranian nature reserve. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And Persian leopards, though they are rare and need protection.

visuals: A rare Asiatic cheetah prowling through the arid desert landscape of central Iran. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Just like the Asiatic cheetah, a critically endangered subspecies that’s exclusively found in the Iranian deserts.

visuals: A busy street in Tehran, Iran, with the snow-capped Alborz mountains rising in the background. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Tehran is the capital city and it’s huge! It’s super busy and surrounded by snow-capped mountains. And listen to this, its area has been inhabited for over 6000 years!

visuals: The ancient ruins of Persepolis in Iran, with its massive stone columns and intricate carvings from the Persian Empire. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: In fact, Iran is one of the oldest civilizations on Earth! Cities like Persepolis go back 2,500 years.

visuals: The Golestan Palace gardens in Iran bustling with people and inhabitants. Open space, not closed. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Most Iranians speak Persian (also known as Farsi.) It's one of the oldest languages still spoken today. But guess what? People also speak Kurdish, Azeri, Luri, and more. It's like a language party!

visuals: Naqsh-e Jahan Square in Isfahan in Iran bustling with people and inhabitants. Open space, not closed. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: About 89 million people live in Iran, almost the same as the entire population of Mexico!

visuals: A platter of fragrant, bright yellow Iranian saffron rice topped with barberries and pistachio slivers. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Feeling hungry? Iranian food is bursting with color and flavor! One popular dish is saffron rice: bright yellow, spice-tastic, and often topped with crunchy bits. Mmm.

visuals: Succulent Iranian lamb and chicken kebabs served on a platter with grilled tomatoes and flatbread. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Add some juicy kebabs and you've got a plate ready for a royal feast!

visuals: A glass of refreshing Iranian doogh (yogurt drink) with dried mint leaves, served on a traditional wooden table. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Thirsty? Try a classic Iranian yogurt drink called “doogh”. It’s cold, salty, and really refreshing.

visuals: A steaming bowl of traditional Iranian aash (thick herb soup) with noodles, beans, and a swirl of yogurt on top. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And in colder months, everyone slurps up warm aash. It’s a thick, herby soup with noodles and lentils.

visuals: A traditional Haft-Seen table for the Iranian Nowruz (New Year) with the seven symbolic items, flowers, and sweets. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: When spring arrives, it’s party time! Nowruz, the Persian New Year, brings dancing, fire-jumping, and sweet treats.

visuals: Iranian musicians playing traditional string instruments like the tar and setar in a historic Persian courtyard. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And Persian classical music? Wow! Instruments like the tar and setar sing ancient stories. It's like history doing a solo.

visuals: A framed portrait of Iranian soccer legend Ali Daei celebrating a goal in his national team jersey. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Iran has played in several World Cups since 1978. Ali Daei, was the first male player in football history to surpass 100 international goals, a record he held for nearly two decades until Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi surpassed him recently.

visuals: A vibrant, handwoven Persian rug with intricate floral patterns and rich colors displayed in a traditional workshop. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And we haven't even talked about carpets yet! Persian rugs are world-famous. People admire them for their detailed patterns and vibrant colors, and many are still handwoven. Some are even considered masterpieces, like artwork you walk on!

visuals: A passenger plane flying over the vast and varied landscape of Iran, from mountains to deserts. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: I would love to have a magic carpet to continue this trip, but this plane will have to do. Until next time!
